% SCI-PTC v0.1 shared falsifiable predictions -- owner-review candidate r0.5.
\section{Falsifiable edge predictions}
\label{sec:normative-predictions}

These are scientific oracles for later conformance and validation work. They
are not claims that an implementation has passed.

\PTCPrediction{001}{RTC-terminal disabled route}{Rationale 8.3}{D005,WP1-D005}{SCI-RTC}{With PTC explicitly disabled, complete required RTC publication is followed by successful Citlali termination; CAL, PTC, and MAP are not entered and no product states for those stages are fabricated. Failure of required RTC publication fails the route.}
\PTCPrediction{002}{Same-unit response loss}{Rationale 1.3}{D002,D014}{SCI-CAL}{A detector-common astronomical perturbation can retain mJy-per-fixed-nominal-beam units while being attenuated or annihilated; unit equality alone will not predict recovered amplitude.}
\PTCPrediction{003}{Correlation non-identification}{Rationale 1.2}{D004,D014}{None}{Two data sets with the same detector covariance but different physical mixtures admit the same fitted correlated subspace; the fit alone cannot distinguish atmosphere from sky or electronics.}
\PTCPrediction{004}{Gauge invariance}{Rationale 3.1}{D014,D015}{None}{Negating a basis/loading pair, reciprocally rescaling it, or rotating a degenerate basis leaves the fitted correlated signal and transformed output unchanged within declared numerical tolerance.}
\PTCPrediction{005}{Centering null mode}{Rationale 3.1 and 7.2}{D017}{None}{In a full-procedure rerun, adding a perturbation wholly in the declared additive-reference mode changes the re-estimated $\lambda$ and not the centered fit coordinate; the newly estimated location is again discarded and the mode remains in the published null-space state. In fixed-state response $\lambda$ is held fixed and the perturbation is propagated by the already-fitted $J_{\Theta}[Y]$.}
\PTCPrediction{006}{Scaling restoration}{Rationale 3.1}{D017}{None}{For an invertible internal scaling multiplied by a finite nonzero constant and consistently inverted, ordinary transformed output in the physical unit is unchanged within tolerance.}
\PTCPrediction{007}{Zero-fill is not exclusion}{Rationale 2.1}{D007,D010}{None}{Replacing one excluded nonzero sample by zero before ordinary PCA changes means/covariance and can change the selected subspace; a correctly masked/weighted missing-data estimator gives zero fit influence instead.}
\PTCPrediction{008}{Fit-excluded apply-allowed}{Rationale 2.1 and 4.2}{D007}{None}{An occurrence excluded from fitting but admitted for application is acted on by the exact frozen application map without affecting learned or selected state; toggling only its output support does not refit.}
\PTCPrediction{009}{Support-stage independence}{Rationale 2.1}{D007}{VAL}{Changing coefficient-only support changes the affected coefficient product but not the fitted basis or transformed signal; changing fit support invalidates or refits the fitted state.}
\PTCPrediction{010}{Influence through fitting}{Rationale 2.2}{D007}{VAL}{A single occurrence used to fit a common mode can influence subtractions at many other occurrences even where its direct local derivative is zero; those outputs carry transitive fit influence.}
\PTCPrediction{011}{Source-mask boundary}{Rationale 3.3}{D004,D014}{AST,ALIGN}{Moving a sample across a declared mask boundary changes fit/application behavior only according to the serialized polarity and boundary rule; unmasked sky remains eligible to project into the removed subspace.}
\PTCPrediction{012}{Configured-group isolation}{Rationale 3.2}{D011,WP1-D006}{None}{Changing data in another array does not change the selected array's result. In network mode, changing one network does not change another network's fitted support, subspace, or kernel operator; in array mode the same change may alter the one array-wide subspace.}
\PTCPrediction{013}{Grouping alternatives}{Rationale 3.2}{D011,WP1-D006}{None}{The same array can yield different removed subspaces under configured network- and array-level PCA because their support and coupling domains differ. Neither result is reproduced by silently applying both levels sequentially.}
\PTCPrediction{014}{Common-mode denominator failure}{Rationale 4.1}{D010}{None}{A group/time with zero, empty, or non-finite admitted denominator yields unavailable/rejected state or a typed fallback, never a silently valid zero common mode.}
\PTCPrediction{015}{Fixed-template orthogonality}{Rationale 4.1}{D010}{None}{For a frozen fixed-template metric, a perturbation exactly orthogonal to the removed subspace is preserved by the conditional operator; learned-template motion is a separate full-procedure effect.}
\PTCPrediction{016}{Rank-deficient gauge}{Rationale 4.1}{D010,D012}{None}{Duplicate or zero columns produce a rank-deficient fit whose generalized inverse, tolerance, selected subspace, and deterministic tie rule reproduce the emitted subtraction.}
\PTCPrediction{017}{Future least-aggressive selection}{Rationale 4.3}{D012,WP1-D007}{Owner policy}{For a separately authorized automatic-selection family with nested candidates where the first two fail at least one required predicate and the third passes all, the third is selected even if an earlier candidate has a better scalar score. The ordinary configured-rank route does not perform this comparison.}
\PTCPrediction{018}{Future no-compensating metric}{Rationale 4.3}{D012,WP1-D007}{Owner policy}{In a separately authorized automatic-selection family, excellent residual suppression cannot compensate for a failed astronomical-transfer predicate. No diagnostic changes the ordinary route's explicitly requested rank.}
\PTCPrediction{019}{Future deterministic tie}{Rationale 4.3}{D012,WP1-D007}{Owner policy}{Two future automatic-selection candidates equal under every required predicate and ordering resolve identically using the registered tie rule. The singleton ordinary candidate has no data-derived tie decision.}
\PTCPrediction{020}{Failed candidate resolution}{Rationale 4.3}{D012,WP1-D007}{Owner policy}{An unrealizable ordinary requested rank produces no transformed signal or map and is not clipped. If no candidate passes a future automatic-selection family, no transformed product claiming that admission is produced.}
\PTCPrediction{021}{Immutable-parent refinement}{Rationale 5.2}{D009,WP1-D008}{SCI-CAL}{The ordinary route emits one immutable-parent fit and no second support-changing fit. In a separately authorized future refinement, a second fit equals a fresh fit of the complete selected model on the immutable CAL parent and differs, in general, from fitting the already cleaned first output.}
\PTCPrediction{022}{Output-only classification}{Rationale 5.2}{D009}{VAL}{Changing one detector from retained to postfit-output-reject without changing fit support preserves the fitted subspace and other detectors' transformed values.}
\PTCPrediction{023}{Refinement oscillation}{Rationale 5.2}{D009,WP1-D008}{Owner policy}{The ordinary route cannot oscillate through support-changing refits because its maximum is zero. A future refinement with alternating high-leverage membership reaches its declared oscillation/exhaustion state and is never labeled converged.}
\PTCPrediction{024}{Diagnostic population dependence}{Rationale 5.1}{D009,WP1-D008}{Owner policy}{The same residual statistic can differ under two declared reference populations, but in the ordinary route neither diagnostic result changes support, configured rank, or resolved model.}
\PTCPrediction{025}{Diagnostic-only $r$ inertia}{Rationale 4.2}{D008,Q001,WP1-D008}{SCI-RTC}{Changing an admitted conditioned-$r$ diagnostic while holding calibrated $x$ and all $x$ policy fixed can change only $r$ diagnostic outputs, not $x$ fit membership, configured or resolved rank, subtraction, output, or coefficients.}
\PTCPrediction{026}{Raw-$r$ incompatibility}{Rationale 4.2}{D008}{SCI-RTC}{If conditioned-$r$ operator, unit, response, optical-leakage state, or exact $x$-grid relation is missing, the $r$ diagnostic branch is unavailable while the admitted $x$ branch may remain defined.}
\PTCPrediction{027}{Coefficient gauge}{Rationale 6.1}{D015}{None}{Reciprocal basis/loading rescaling changes fitted loading values but leaves the modeled subtraction unchanged; an analysis/gridding coefficient does not transform merely because a loading gauge changes.}
\PTCPrediction{028}{Coefficient normalization}{Rationale 6.1}{D015}{SCI-MAP}{Multiplying all raw gridding coefficients by a common nonzero factor can leave a normalized weighted estimate unchanged while changing the denominator, proving that the denominator is not automatically precision.}
\PTCPrediction{029}{Conditional covariance}{Rationale 6.2}{D014}{NOI}{For a fixed analytic $J_{\Theta}[Y]$ and declared $C_Y$, the conditional covariance equals $J_{\Theta}[Y]C_YJ_{\Theta}[Y]^{\mathsf T}$ including off-diagonal detector/time terms.}
\PTCPrediction{030}{Selection variance term}{Rationale 6.2}{D012,D014}{NOI}{Across perturbations that change rank or support, total output variance exceeds or differs from the mean conditional covariance whenever between-selection means vary.}
\PTCPrediction{031}{Fixed companion noninterference}{Rationale 7.1}{D013}{None}{Adding a response companion through the fixed-state path leaves fitted modes, rank, masks, detector classes, and transformed science data unchanged.}
\PTCPrediction{032}{Full-procedure nonlinearity}{Rationale 7.2}{D013}{None}{An injected source that crosses a rank, mask, clipping, classification, or convergence boundary produces amplitude- or side-dependent finite response rather than one global linear kernel.}
\PTCPrediction{033}{Package response boundary}{Rationale 7.2}{D013}{SCI-RTC,SCI-CAL}{Rerunning PTC from a fixed CAL parent can characterize PTC-full-procedure response but cannot expose a changed RTC or CAL learned state; that requires a separately named whole-chain study.}
\PTCPrediction{034}{Map-center factor availability}{Rationale 7.3}{D016}{SCI-MAP,BEAM}{Removing the exact source companion or named reference MAP operator makes the map-center diagnostic unavailable while leaving a supported sample-domain PTC response potentially available.}
\PTCPrediction{035}{Compact versus extended response}{Rationale 7.3}{D016}{BEAM}{A compact source and detector-common extended mode with equal nominal peak amplitude can have different PTC responses; the compact map-center diagnostic cannot predict the extended response.}
\PTCPrediction{036}{Random-state reproducibility}{Rationale 8.2}{D006}{None}{Repeating a simulation or randomized estimator with identical generator/version, seed, stream, and input identity reproduces the declared draws and realized result; changing one stream changes only its assigned draws.}
\PTCPrediction{037}{Required-output atomicity}{Rationale 8.1}{D005}{None}{Failure to publish one required sibling or link leaves the product explicitly incomplete; a remaining readable file cannot be labeled complete.}
\PTCPrediction{038}{Evidence-layer separation}{Rationale 9.2}{D006}{None}{Successful algebraic and document-coverage checks do not change implementation conformity, representation fidelity, observational performance, or production-readiness status from unassessed/not performed.}
\PTCPrediction{039}{Frozen component versus projection}{Rationale 4.2}{D010,Q002,WP1-D001}{None}{For a perturbation with nonzero projection onto the frozen removed subspace, subtraction of the typed frozen total-removed operand has identity derivative while frozen-subspace application removes that projected component; the two responses differ even though both reproduce the fitted-parent transformed result.}
\PTCPrediction{040}{Temporal versus detector action}{Rationale 4.2}{D010,Q002}{None}{For a nonsymmetric response matrix $H$, temporal-left projection $\mathcal L^t_{\Theta}H$ and detector-right projection $H\mathcal L^d_{\Theta}$ generally differ; matrix orientation and rank alone cannot select the propagated companion.}
\PTCPrediction{041}{No double upstream response}{Rationale 7.1}{D013}{SCI-CAL}{Propagating a CAL-grid companion through $J_{\Theta}[Y]$ gives the same result as propagating its source-domain parent through $J_{\Theta}[Y]\circ K_{\rm up\to CAL}$ exactly once; applying $K_{\rm up\to CAL}$ again changes the domain or value and is rejected.}
\PTCPrediction{042}{Typed procedure state change}{Rationale 7.2}{D013}{None}{A perturbation that changes selected rank or learned centering location yields a valid transformed-signal finite difference and separate typed state changes; attempting to subtract the complete procedure tuples is undefined and cannot produce the response.}
\PTCPrediction{043}{Candidate-evidence reconstruction}{Rationale 4.1 and 4.3}{D012}{Owner policy}{Given the retained candidate order, fitted states, predicate values, causes, and tie rule, the selected or rejected disposition is reproduced exactly; removing one failed predicate record makes the selection audit incomplete.}
\PTCPrediction{044}{External-parent fail-closed}{Rationale 3.3}{D004,D014}{FRUIT}{Removing the recurrence identity or coordinate registration from an otherwise numerical source/residual parent makes the affected protected or fitted role unavailable while leaving independent PTC roles unchanged.}
\PTCPrediction{045}{Surrogate support transformation}{Rationale 8.2}{D006,D007}{VAL shared semantics,NOI}{Shifting surrogate signal without shifting its associated facts, causes, support decisions, boundaries, and identity changes the admitted population and fails the surrogate contract; shifting them together reproduces the declared transformed membership, while insufficient support is rejected rather than zero-filled.}
\PTCPrediction{046}{Astronomical-predicate typing}{Rationale 4.3}{D012,D013}{Owner policy}{Two candidates with the same scalar transfer value but different source class, response type, amplitude/location domain, or uncertainty treatment do not satisfy the same astronomical-transfer predicate and cannot be substituted.}
\PTCPrediction{047}{Unavailable bias claim}{Rationale 6.2}{D010,D014}{NOI}{When an estimator family supplies no expectation/bias statement for data-dependent selection, the bias claim remains unavailable even if one synthetic realization has zero measured residual mean.}
\PTCPrediction{048}{Independent product and response states}{Rationale 8.3}{D005,D013,WP1-D005}{None}{A realized transformed signal can coexist with unavailable complete response. The RTC-terminal route never enters PTC and therefore has no PTC response axis to encode; neither condition can be inferred from the other.}

\PTCPrediction{049}{Undefined fit-excluded extension}{Rationale 4.2}{D007,D010}{None}{For a fit-excluded occurrence missing any basis coefficient or coefficient-recomputation input, neighboring support, detector binding, metric term, coordinate transform, or boundary state required by the resolved operator, application is unavailable. Filling, interpolating, or reconstructing that occurrence changes the declared operator and cannot reproduce the authorized fit-excluded/apply-allowed result.}

\PTCPrediction{050}{Conservative support composition}{Rationale 2.1}{D007}{PTC and named-use owners}{For an exact PTC-owned use, adding an applicable excluding cause to otherwise permitting facts changes the composite result to ineligible and cannot be rescued by another permitting cause. With no known exclusion but one unknown required predicate, the result is \texttt{decision\_unavailable}; supplying that predicate as true can then make the result eligible without erasing any cause.}

\PTCPrediction{051}{Network support isolation}{Rationale 2.1 and 3.2}{WP1-D006}{None}{In network mode, changing fit or application support in one network changes only that network's fitted or applied state; every other network's $\Theta_g$ and propagated kernel remain identical.}

\PTCPrediction{052}{Array cross-network coupling}{Rationale 3.2}{WP1-D006}{None}{In array mode, changing admitted data in one network can change the one array-wide loading subspace and therefore the transformed data or kernel in another network within the same array.}

\PTCPrediction{053}{Rank-zero failure}{Rationale 4.3 and 8.3}{WP1-D005,D007}{None}{A request with $k=0$ yields an explicit failed PTC resolution, no centering-only output, no RTC-export route conversion, and no map.}

\PTCPrediction{054}{Unrealizable-rank failure}{Rationale 4.3 and 8.2}{WP1-D007}{None}{A positive rank exceeding exact group-local feasibility yields failure with group and cause; the emitted state contains no clipped or substituted rank and no transformed output.}

\PTCPrediction{055}{Configured-rank reproducibility}{Rationale 4.3}{WP1-D007}{None}{Repeated resolution of the same CAL parent, configured group, support, masks, metric, degeneracy tolerance, and positive requested rank reproduces the same removed subspace and operator within declared numerical tolerance.}

\PTCPrediction{056}{Full-support projector reduction}{Rationale 4.2}{WP1-D006}{None}{When every detector in a group has uniform application influence, the mask-aware coefficient solve reduces within tolerance to detector-right projection through $I-\widehat A_g(\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T}\widehat A_g)^+\widehat A_g^{\mathsf T}$.}

\PTCPrediction{057}{Masked influence is not zero data}{Rationale 2.1 and 4.2}{WP1-D006}{None}{Changing the numerical value stored at an application-excluded detector while keeping its influence zero leaves the time-local coefficient solve unchanged; changing its influence to admitted can change the solve. Replacing the excluded value by an admitted numerical zero need not reproduce either result.}

\PTCPrediction{058}{Data-kernel state identity}{Rationale 7.1}{WP1-D001,D006,D008}{SCI-CAL}{For fixed $\Theta_g$, applying the group-local linear operator to a compatible kernel uses the same support, mask, metric, rank, subspace, generalized inverse, and tolerance as the data, leaves all learned state unchanged, and does not subtract $\lambda_g$ from the perturbation.}

\PTCPrediction{059}{Advisory-diagnostic inertia}{Rationale 5.1--5.2}{WP1-D008}{None}{Changing an ordinary post-fit advisory diagnostic while holding the immutable CAL parent and resolved operator state fixed changes only that diagnostic record; support, rank, $\Theta_g$, transformed data, and propagated kernel remain unchanged.}
